chapter: Learning the drums and early influences
title: Arguing with Sy Oliver over two beats and four beats
summary: Crawford recalls arguments with Sy Oliver about riding out the last chorus in four versus two, and how Sy still hired him on every date.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But you never know. Maybe I did occasionally, due to the fact that, if I want to make it full, and I'd drop jump on four-four full force, everything. Sy Oliver and I used to have some -- quite frequently had some heated arguments about that four-four and two-four bit.

Sy, when the band was going out, why Sy contributed a lot to that Lurcefurt Lurcefurt band. When we were "going home" as we used to say, that means last chorus course-going out, close the door in their face, Sy would tell me for two beats. Now, when you riding out, you want to send them out, you know. And so we would have some heated arguments.
So he came to me and said, what's wrong with two beats? Why don't you want to play it? I see it in your face. I says, Sy, what's wrong with two beats is there are two beats missing.
Oh, yes wed argue (Inaudible), but we'd kiss and make up, and so Sy would call me for every record date that he'd arrange and supervise.
